questions.qText: If a complex number z satisfies |z|^2 + \frac{4}{|z|^2} - 2\left(\frac{z}{\bar z}+\frac{\bar z}{z}\right) -16 = 0, then the maximum value of |z| is
questions.sText: Let z=r(\cos\theta+i\sin\theta). Then \frac{z}{\bar z}+\frac{\bar z}{z}=2\cos2\theta. Substituting gives r^2+\frac{4}{r^2}-4\cos2\theta-16=0 \Rightarrow r^4-4r^2(\cos2\theta+4)+4=0. Maximum r occurs when \cos2\theta=1 giving r=2+\sqrt{6}.

questions.qText: If z^2+(p+iq)z+r+is=0 where p,q,r,s are non-zero has real roots, then
questions.sText: Let root z=x+iy be real so y=0. From (x+iy)^2+(p+iq)(x+iy)+r+is=0 equate real and imaginary parts. Solving gives x=-s/q and substituting back gives pqs=s^2+rq^2.

questions.sText: Using 1+z+z^2+z^3+z^4=0 for 5th roots of unity. Rearranging terms gives expression =5z^4.

questions.qText: If z=\frac{1}{2}(\sqrt3-i), then the least possible integral value of m such that (z^{101}+i^{109})^{106}=z^{m+1} is
questions.sText: z=\frac{1}{2}(\sqrt3-i)=i\omega^2 where \omega is imaginary cube root of unity. Simplifying (z^{101}+i^{109})^{106}=(i\omega^2)^{m+1}. Solving gives m=9.

questions.qText: Number of imaginary complex numbers satisfying z^2=\bar z\,2^{1-|z|}
questions.sText: Given z^2=\bar z\,2^{1-|z|}. Taking modulus gives |z|^3=1 so |z|=1. Substituting gives two imaginary solutions.

questions.qText: If arg(z^{3/8})=\frac12 arg(z^2+\bar z^{1/2}), then which of the following is never true?
questions.sText: Using argument relations gives arg(z^{3/4})=arg(z^2+\bar z^{1/2}). Simplifying leads to condition z=\bar z or z=1. Hence Re(z)=0 is impossible.

questions.qText: Consider the circle |z-5i|=3 and two points z1 and z2 on it such that |z1|<|z2| and Arg(z1)=Arg(z2)=\pi/3. A tangent at z2 cuts the real axis at z3. Which statement is not true?
questions.sText: Using geometry of circle |z-5i|=3 and tangent properties gives relations for intersection with real axis. Checking options shows |z3|=2\sqrt3 is false.

questions.qText: If z1,z2,z3 are any three roots of z^6=(z+1)^6 then arg((z1-z3)/(z2-z3)) can be equal to
questions.sText: From z^6=(z+1)^6 we get |z|=|z+1| so roots lie on perpendicular bisector of segment joining 0 and -1. Hence points are collinear giving argument ratio 0 or \pi.

questions.qText: If the imaginary part of \frac{z-3}{e^{i\theta}}+\frac{e^{i\theta}}{z-3} is zero then z lies on
questions.sText: Let z-3=re^{i\phi}. Substitution gives imaginary part condition leading to r=1 or sin(\phi-\theta)=0 which represents unit circle centered at 3 and line through (3,0).

questions.sText: Manipulating equation gives if w1 is root then 1/\bar w1 also root. Hence roots lie on unit circle implying |w1|=|w2|=1.

questions.qText: Let z1,z2,z3 be vertices of triangle ABC such that (z3-z2)/(z1-z2) is purely imaginary. A square on AC is drawn outward and its center is z4. Then which are true?
questions.sText: Center of square implies AP=PC and angle APC=\pi/2. Using argument relations gives arg((z1-z2)/(z4-z2))=-\alpha and arg((z3-z2)/(z4-z2))=\alpha whose sum is zero. Also points are concyclic.

questions.sText: From |Z1|=|Z2| and |Z1+Z2|=|Z1| we get angle between Z1 and Z2 is 120°. Hence Z1/Z2 equals cube roots of unity except 1.

questions.qText: Let z1,z2,z3 be distinct complex numbers with |z1|=|z2|=|z3|=1. Which statements are true?
questions.sText: Using |zi|=1 properties and algebraic manipulation of symmetric expressions leads to results (B),(C),(D).

questions.sText: Points on circle radius 4 with zero vector sum imply symmetric configuration leading to rectangle. Maximum area occurs for perpendicular diagonals giving 32.

questions.qText: Let z1,z2,z3 be three distinct complex numbers satisfying |z1|=|z2|=|z3|=1. Which are true?
questions.sText: Using unit modulus properties and symmetry relations gives (B),(C),(D) true.

questions.qText: If a,b are complex numbers and one root of x^2+ax+b=0 is purely real and the other purely imaginary and a^2-\bar a^2=kb then find k.
questions.sText: Let roots be \alpha (real) and i\beta (imaginary). Then \alpha+i\beta=-a and \alpha i\beta=b. From relations obtain 4i\alpha\beta=a^2-\bar a^2=4b giving k=4.

questions.qText: Let 1, \omega and \omega^2 be cube roots of unity. The least possible degree of a polynomial with real coefficients having 2\omega^2, 3+4\omega, 3+4\omega^2 and 5-\omega-\omega^2 as roots is
questions.sText: Complex roots occur with conjugates for real coefficients. Counting required conjugates gives minimum 5 roots hence degree 5.

questions.qText: If \omega is imaginary cube root of unity then number of integer pairs (a,b) such that |a\omega+b|=1 is
questions.sText: |a\omega+b|^2=(a\omega+b)(a\omega^2+b)=a^2-ab+b^2=1. Integer solutions of this quadratic form give 6 pairs.

questions.qText: If \alpha,\beta,\gamma are roots of x^3-3x^2+3x+7=0 and \omega is cube root of unity then |(\alpha-1)/(\beta-1)+(\beta-1)/(\gamma-1)+(\gamma-1)/(\alpha-1)| equals
questions.sText: x^3-3x^2+3x+7=0 ⇒ (x-1)^3=-8 so roots are -1,1-2\omega,1-2\omega^2. Substituting gives magnitude 3.

questions.qText: Complex numbers z1,z2 satisfy |z1|=2 and |z2|=3. If angle between their vectors is 60° then value of 19|(z1-z2)/(z1+z2)|^2 is
questions.sText: Using |z1\pm z2|^2=|z1|^2+|z2|^2\pm2|z1||z2|\cos60°. Compute ratio giving result 7.

questions.sText: Using \omega^2+\omega+1=0 and simplifying fractions transforms expression leading to cancellation of terms giving 0.
